title: Job 1 raid timing and Job 19 hard words
english: On Job 1 the Selecta mark how the Accuser ordered the raid: camels under the horsemen, donkeys and ox-teams under the captors, sheep under fire because he hated them, and the sons targeted whenever he found a time. Had he found them reading or praying, Origen says, he would have had no place to strike; he prevailed when the moment was drunkenness and the drinking-party. The wind that struck the houses corners is read with the hypocrites who pray on street corners: whoever has left the straight road lives by corners, and a broad corner is large, loose wickedness.

On Job 19, How long will you weary my soul? heavy words work like heavy loads on beasts. Baldads speech felt like a crushing pack, and nothing reaches a soul like a hard word — many endure bodily torture who cannot endure insult. The finished athlete still endures while weary; to bear insult is greatness, as Paul says, Being reviled, we bless. Job remains the bravest of athletes, yet he feels the fatigue of harsh oversight and asks why friends add soul-pain to body-pain, wounding more with speech than disease wounds flesh.

You speak against me names shameless face-to-face insult. I cry out and nowhere is judgment means the bout is not finished: the crowns verdict does not come mid-wrestling. Origen will not accuse God that Job suffers without sentence; judgment here is freedom and release. Chapter 20 then turns to gifts going up to heaven and the heretics lofty sacrifice, and to dreamlike enemies who invent faults and vanish like smoke in the psalm.
